overall: The AG found the Selectboard did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the October 9 notice topics, including the ARPA acronym, were sufficiently specific. The minutes claim was declined as raised first on review.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 9 meeting notice topics were insufficiently specific to advise the public of the issues to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: After review, we are satisfied that each of the notice topics identified in the instant complaint were sufficiently specific, and the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the Board did not answer his requests for more detail on the Halloween road closure and Highway/Fire involvement, which he said were not in prior years.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, although we encourage public bodies to be responsive to the residents they represent, the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body provide additional detail regarding discussion topics upon request, provided that the meeting notice is otherwise sufficient.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged use of the acronym ARPA on the notice was ambiguous and rendered the notice insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we are satisfied that the acronym “ARPA” has become widely used over the past few years as shorthand for the American Rescue Plan Act

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the special Town Meeting warrant language, and the jargon used to correct the tax-rate certification error, was unclear.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government does not review the sufficiency or clarity of Town Meeting warrants, see OML 2025-40, and we note that the Board did not engage in a substantive discussion of the warrant or the warrant language.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice for the telecommunication tower lease award was insufficient because the Board could not answer whether cellular carriers would change.
allegations.key_passage: Where the Board did not discuss the carriers, the meeting notice was not insufficient for not including this detail.

allegations.summary: In a request for further review, complainant alleged the October 9 minutes were unclear and lacked detail; this was not raised in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We do not review allegations raised for the first time in a request for further review that were not raised in a complaint filed with the public body.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
